memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"But select capable men from all the people-men who fear God, trustworthy men who
hate dishonest gain-and appoint them as officials over thousands, hundreds,
fifties and tens." - Ex 18:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at the job description. Four qualities, and only one of them is about
ability.

Capable. Fearing God. Trustworthy. Hating dishonest gain.

Three of the four are about character. That is a striking ratio, and it runs
against how most of us select people. We tend to look first at competence and
hope character will be adequate. Jethro reverses the emphasis.

"Hate dishonest gain" is especially pointed. These men would be judges, deciding
disputes, and a judge who can be bought destroys justice for everyone,
particularly the poor who cannot afford to compete.

Notice the structure too: thousands, hundreds, fifties, tens. Right down to
groups of ten. That means most people's disputes were handled by someone who
actually knew them, someone local and accessible.

Paul's lists of qualifications for church leadership follow the same pattern.
Read 1 Timothy 3 and notice how little is about talent and how much is about
character, temperament, and household life. "Not a lover of money," he writes
(1 Tim 3:3), echoing this very verse.

God has always cared more about who a leader is than what a leader can do.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When you assess people, do you weigh character as heavily as competence?
2. Would you meet these four qualifications yourself?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, build character in me, not just capability. Make me trustworthy in the
things nobody sees. Amen.
